A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same UniPart research, with matching methods, equations, and identifiable figures and tables. The comparison includes v3's supplementary Sections S1–S3; the supplied v2 contains no supplementary section.

before.justification: V2 reports original generation and segmentation evaluations in Tables 1–2, reconstruction examples, and component ablations.

after.justification: V3 reports original generation, reconstruction, and segmentation results in Tables 1–2 and S1, alongside qualitative comparisons and analyses.

M1.justification: The Geom-Seg VAE, whole-level flow model, latent segmentation, and dual-space part diffusion retain the same procedures and objectives in Section 3 and Equations 1–5. S1 newly discloses architectural and decoder details without establishing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use ABO, Objaverse, and Objaverse-XL for the same object-generation and segmentation scope, with geometry reconstruction evaluation. Additional examples and comparisons do not establish a new dataset, domain, or distinct task; newly disclosed filtering details do not demonstrate changed coverage.

E2.justification: V3 expands reconstruction comparison beyond Hunyuan3D-2.1 by reporting TRELLIS, Dora, Craftsman, and XCubes in Table 2. Figure S3 also introduces an unnamed commercial comparator. The five generation baselines and three segmentation baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 drops F@0.05 and adds IoU, while new reconstruction Table 2 reports CD and F1@0.01. Mesh normalization and rotation selection remain unchanged. V3 omits the explicit 100-object generation test-set description and reports 300K rather than 302K training objects, without establishing resampling or reruns.

E4.justification: V3 adds attention-based latent correlation analysis (Figure 1), quantitative reconstruction-preservation evidence (Table 2), and a structural-complexity failure case (Figure 8). It removes v2's global-conditioning and latent-versus-point-conditioning ablations in Figure 7. The canonical-space, local-attention, and space-embedding ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained segmentation evaluation uses the same annotation procedure without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all generation scores: for example, UniPart's F-score at 0.1 changes from 0.8052 to 92.21 on a ×100 scale, without sufficient protocol detail to establish a same-setting gain. New IoU scores place UniPart at 21.99, below XPart (31.95), OmniPart (27.94), and HoloPart (23.40). Reconstruction and commercial-comparison results are added, while Table S1 preserves all four earlier segmentation scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–5 are substantively unchanged. The appendix supplies implementation explanations, not new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified geometry-segmentation latents, two-stage generation, dual-space fidelity, and superior part-level generation. New supporting evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 replaces the introduction's compression/DINOv2 explanation of emergent part awareness with an attention-correlation interpretation and adds an FPS-based explanation of token locality in S1. It adds a concrete high-complexity failure condition while removing the earlier scene-generation and voxel-latent limitations. The principal interpretations of the method remain.

D1.justification: New S1 substantially expands implementation documentation: MoE architecture, DINOv2 conditioning, an eight-layer latent-conditioning block, randomized part-ID embeddings, mask decoding, and position recovery. It also specifies vertex-merging tolerance, small-part filtering, permitted part counts, and manual data review. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated procedural changes; optimizer and hardware settings remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Dora, XCube, and Hunyuan-DiT for comparisons and implementation context. The related-work taxonomy and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; TRELLIS and DINOv2 bibliographic updates do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites portions of the motivation, dataset description, and conclusion, moves segmentation evaluation into S2, and adds supplementary organization, acknowledgements, and affiliation updates. Most abstract, related-work, and method prose and the main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds correlation and failure figures, a reconstruction table, and a commercial-comparison figure; restructures Table 1; and removes the conditioning-ablation figure. Earlier generation examples are redistributed and expanded across supplementary galleries, and the segmentation table moves to S1. The pipeline and principal qualitative baseline comparison are retained.

improvement.justification: S1 substantially improves implementation transparency, Figure 1 supports the part-awareness motivation, and Figure 8 documents failures. However, v3 removes two conditioning ablations and the explicit generation test size, replaces central numerical results without explaining their comparability, and leaves unfavorable IoU rankings undiscussed. These unresolved changes to the central empirical evidence prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite the documentation gains.
